raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`top_k_top_p_min_p_sampling_from_probs_torch` sorts the whole vocabulary on every decode step and then zeroes every column at rank `>= top_k`:

```python
probs_sort, probs_idx = probs.sort(dim=-1, descending=True)
...
probs_sort[torch.arange(0, probs.shape[-1], ...).view(1, -1) >= top_ks.view(-1, 1)] = 0.0
```

On ROCm this is the default sampler, not a fallback: `is_flashinfer_available()` requires CUDA, so `sampling_backend` resolves to `pytorch`. Any request with a finite `top_k` takes this path. Through the OpenAI-compatible endpoints the model's `generation_config` supplies one by default, e.g. `top_k=20` for the Qwen3 / Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 families. With vocabularies of 152k–248k tokens the full sort dominates the sampler.

## Modifications

- When every row has a finite `top_k`, sort only the `max(top_k)` leading columns with `torch.topk(..., sorted=True)`. Every column past each row's `top_k` is zeroed afterwards anyway, so the leading `max(top_k)` columns hold all the mass that survives: the top-p cumulative sum, the min-p threshold (`probs_sort[:, 0]`) and the sampled token are unchanged.
- The bound is a host-side field, `SamplingBatchInfo.max_top_k`, built from the request params next to `npu_top_k_top_p_eligible`, so the sampler adds no device-to-host sync. It is `None` when any row samples from the whole vocabulary. `merge_batch` takes the max (or `None`); `filter_batch` keeps it unchanged, since any upper bound stays exact. `SamplingBatchInfo` objects built elsewhere (e.g. the EAGLE draft CUDA graph) leave it `None` and keep the full sort.
- Two paths keep the full sort:
  - The seeded path (deterministic inference). The bound is batch-wide, and the order `topk` gives tied probabilities may depend on `k`; deterministic results must not depend on batch composition.
  - `return_filtered_probs=True`, whose sorted tensors are handed to the sampling-mask capture.

Related: #33539 (open) changes this function to keep tokens tied with the k-th probability. Those can sit past rank `max(top_k)`, so if both land, the bound needs to cover the tie set.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/unit/sampling/test_torch_sampling_top_k_bound.py` (new, CPU): with `torch.multinomial` replaced by argmax, the bounded sort yields the same tokens and exactly the same weights as the leading `max(top_k)` columns of the full sort, and the full sort's remaining columns are all zero. It covers mixed per-row `top_k`, top-p and min-p, plus `return_filtered_probs` and a bound at the vocabulary size keeping the full width.
- `test_sampling_batch_info.py`: `max_top_k` construction, merge and filter.
- `test/registered/unit/sampling/`: 216 passed.

End to end on MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.0, torch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0; sglang `main` @ `3ab142adc4` with a `sgl-kernel` build from the same tree and AITER `e7d2453f` (pinned in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`). Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP1, default server args (`sampling_backend=pytorch`).

GSM8K, all 1319 questions, chat API, `temperature=0.7, top_p=0.95, top_k=20`:

| | GSM8K | Output tok/s during the eval |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 0.482 | 4392 |
| This PR | 0.496 | 5703 |

The difference is within sampling noise (std ≈ 0.014). The absolute score is low because the model thinks by default and the eval's 2048-token cap truncates many answers; both runs use the identical harness.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Function microbenchmark, `triton.testing.do_bench` (median), minimum of 5 repetitions, one idle MI355X:

| Vocab | Batch | `top_k=20, top_p=0.95` full / bounded (ms) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 151936 | 1 | 0.189 / 0.151 | 1.25x |
| 151936 | 8 | 0.716 / 0.155 | 4.63x |
| 151936 | 64 | 1.387 / 0.224 | 6.19x |
| 151936 | 256 | 5.140 / 0.446 | 11.52x |
| 248320 | 1 | 0.234 / 0.181 | 1.29x |
| 248320 | 8 | 1.013 / 0.209 | 4.85x |
| 248320 | 64 | 2.089 / 0.273 | 7.67x |
| 248320 | 256 | 8.419 / 0.651 | 12.93x |

`top_k=50, top_p=1.0` gives the same picture (1.21x–15.82x).

Serving, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (vocab 248320), `bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1.0`, `num_prompts = 4 × concurrency`, sampling params `temperature=0.7, top_k=20, top_p=0.95`:

| Concurrency | Median TPOT `main` (ms) | Median TPOT this PR (ms) | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 6.40 | 5.66 | +12.1% |
| 32 | 11.03 | 9.92 | +9.4% |
| 64 | 15.59 | 13.82 | +11.5% |
| 128 | 26.29 | 19.03 | +35.2% |

Greedy requests, and requests without `top_k`, do not reach this code and are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+"""The bounded top-k sort in the torch sampler must match the full vocabulary sort."""
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.sampler import top_k_top_p_min_p_sampling_from_probs_torch
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+VOCAB_SIZE = 4096
+BATCH_SIZE = 8
+
+
+def _probs(seed: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    return torch.softmax(
+        torch.randn(BATCH_SIZE, VOCAB_SIZE, generator=gen) * 3.0, dim=-1
+    )
+
+
+def _run(probs, top_ks, top_ps, min_ps, need_min_p, max_top_k):
+    """Return (token ids, the weights handed to multinomial).
+
+    multinomial is replaced by argmax so both sorts can be compared on the same draw.
+    """
+    seen = {}
+
+    def _argmax(weights, num_samples):
+        seen["weights"] = weights.clone()
+        return weights.argmax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+
+    with mock.patch("torch.multinomial", side_effect=_argmax):
+        token_ids = top_k_top_p_min_p_sampling_from_probs_torch(
+            probs.clone(),
+            top_ks,
+            top_ps,
+            min_ps,
+            need_min_p,
+            None,
+            torch.zeros(BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64),
+            max_top_k=max_top_k,
+        )
+    return token_ids, seen["weights"]
+
+
+class TestTorchSamplingTopKBound(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_bounded_sort_matches_full_sort(self):
+        cases = (
+            # (top_ks, top_ps, min_ps, need_min_p)
+            ([20] * BATCH_SIZE, [1.0] * BATCH_SIZE, [0.0] * BATCH_SIZE, False),
+            (
+                [1, 2, 5, 20, 50, 100, 7, 64],
+                [1.0] * BATCH_SIZE,
+                [0.0] * BATCH_SIZE,
+                False,
+            ),
+            ([20] * BATCH_SIZE, [0.95, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0] * 2, [0.0] * BATCH_SIZE, False),
+            ([40] * BATCH_SIZE, [0.9] * BATCH_SIZE, [0.0, 0.05] * 4, True),
+        )
+        for i, (top_ks, top_ps, min_ps, need_min_p) in enumerate(cases):
+            with self.subTest(case=i):
+                probs = _probs(seed=i)
+                top_ks = torch.tensor(top_ks, dtype=torch.int32)
+                top_ps = torch.tensor(top_ps, dtype=torch.float32)
+                min_ps = torch.tensor(min_ps, dtype=torch.float32)
+                max_top_k = int(top_ks.max())
+
+                full_ids, full_weights = _run(
+                    probs, top_ks, top_ps, min_ps, need_min_p, max_top_k=None
+                )
+                bounded_ids, bounded_weights = _run(
+                    probs, top_ks, top_ps, min_ps, need_min_p, max_top_k=max_top_k
+                )
+
+                self.assertEqual(full_weights.shape[-1], VOCAB_SIZE)
+                self.assertEqual(bounded_weights.shape[-1], max_top_k)
+                self.assertTrue(torch.all(full_weights[:, max_top_k:] == 0))
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    bounded_weights, full_weights[:, :max_top_k], rtol=0, atol=0
+                )
+                torch.testing.assert_close(bounded_ids, full_ids, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+    def test_return_filtered_probs_keeps_full_sort(self):
+        probs = _probs(seed=0)
+        top_ks = torch.full((BATCH_SIZE,), 20, dtype=torch.int32)
+
+        _, filtered_probs, token_ids, _ = top_k_top_p_min_p_sampling_from_probs_torch(
+            probs.clone(),
+            top_ks,
+            torch.ones(BATCH_SIZE),
+            torch.zeros(BATCH_SIZE),
+            False,
+            None,
+            torch.zeros(BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64),
+            return_filtered_probs=True,
+            max_top_k=20,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(filtered_probs.shape[-1], VOCAB_SIZE)
+        self.assertEqual(token_ids.shape[-1], VOCAB_SIZE)
+
+    def test_bound_at_or_above_vocab_keeps_full_sort(self):
+        probs = _probs(seed=0)
+        top_ks = torch.full((BATCH_SIZE,), VOCAB_SIZE, dtype=torch.int32)
+        _, weights = _run(
+            probs,
+            top_ks,
+            torch.ones(BATCH_SIZE),
+            torch.zeros(BATCH_SIZE),
+            False,
+            max_top_k=VOCAB_SIZE,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(weights.shape[-1], VOCAB_SIZE)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
